executive_summary:
Strict score is 73.1, the all-time high, after the Test health jump from 0 to 44.6. That one move carried the cycle. Almost every subjective dimension slid 3 to 8 points two scans ago and has not recovered, and the last scan also dropped File health (97.4 to 89.4), Code quality (98.5 to 94.1) and Duplication (100 to 97.8), so new code in the v4 home is adding mechanical debt while old debt is worked.

Execution is the main problem. 138 of 156 queue items were skipped as temporary (88.5% skip rate), only 8 were resolved and no commits were recorded. Every subjective dimension shows a resolve-then-reopen loop at the repo root: items resolved last cycle came back under new ids (driver_state_module_singletons to driver_module_singleton_state, left_flag_read_at_import to hero_left_flag_import_snapshot, quote_photo_index_vs_key to quote_photo_index_not_key, week_first_clicks_foreign_dom to week_first_dom_click, drivers_rewrite_react_text_nodes to motion_overwrites_react_owned_nodes, v4_home_under_v3_mt to v4_home_in_v3_mt_folder, changelog_in_comments to changelog_in_comments_hero_motion). Those were marked resolved without the root fix landing.

The 94 open review items collapse into about six root causes in components/v3/mt: module-scope driver state, scattered URL flag parsing, the HTML dataset attribute bus, dead dock and state fields in the hero driver, index-vs-key option contracts (quote, covers, bookrow, film titles), and the intro run monolith. Fix each root once, behaviour-identical, with a test, and the score moves across 5 to 8 dimensions per fix. Small, finished clusters beat a long queue that gets skipped.
observe_guidance: Do not trust prior resolved status in components/v3/mt. Seven items resolved last cycle reappeared under new ids, so verify each open review item against the current code before keeping it, and check whether a resolved sibling already claims to cover it. Verification is wasted on the 270 smells and on Security or Duplication; spend it on the six root causes (driver singleton state, flag parsing, HTML attribute bus, hero dead fields and dock modes, index-vs-key contracts, intro run monolith). Flag any item whose fix would change visible motion, timing or flags as owner-decision, not a defect.
reflect_guidance: Focus on Test health first (headroom 55, heaviest weight), then the 22-weight elegance dimensions and Design coherence, Contracts and Type safety, which all point at the same mt driver code. Treat cross-dimension duplicates as one item: hero_state_dead_fields appears in abstraction, design and low elegance; covers_nonnull_then_filter in contracts, type safety and logic; bookrow_key_duplicates_slug in abstraction and type safety; driver singleton state in five dimensions. Constraint: a cluster counts as done only when the root is removed in code and a test pins it, otherwise it reopens next review. Avoid flag deletion and any motion-visible change.
organize_guidance: Order by root cause, not dimension. 1) Tests for mt motion layer, intro timing and engine progress math, written against current behaviour so later refactors are safe. 2) Driver state: one pattern for module-scope state across drivers. 3) One flag reader for URL trial flags (parse once, keep every flag working). 4) Hero driver: remove dead state fields and retired dock spring paths that no flag can reach. 5) Key-not-index contracts for quote options, covers, bookrow and film dress maps. 6) Split intro run and add the throw-safe unlock. Keep clusters to 3 to 8 items each so they finish. Do not re-cluster already-resolved ids, and do not schedule the smells sweep.
sense_check_guidance: Value traps: renaming and comment-only edits that a fresh review rewords and reopens; flag removals the owner wants kept; refactors of hero or intro that shift timing on a site judged by eye. Rework risk is highest where a resolved item already has a near-identical open twin; require the fix to delete the underlying pattern, not move it. Reject any cluster that cannot be tested or checked without a visual pass, or mark it owner-review. A cluster that leaves File health or Code quality worse (new large files, new smells) is a net loss even if a subjective item closes.
